## Pieces

Display lines are grouped into render pieces. A piece closes after a
word holding a daṇḍa, so the two pādas of a hemistich printed as two
lines render as one piece, as Vāgdhenu expects. Prose closes too at
`max_syll` akṣaras; verse closes before a line that would pass
`max_verse`. Each piece keeps `(line, word)` for every word, so timings
can go back to the lines; a word that cleans to nothing (a daṇḍa, a
verse number) stays, untimed.


*Per line, `dict(s, e, w)` from the pieces’ word timings; None for a
line with no words.*

``` python
ps = [[(0,'क'), (0,'ख'), (1,'ग')], [(1,'॥')]]
lt = line_times(3, ps, [[['क',0,100], ['ख',100,200], ['ग',300,400]], [['॥',400,400]]])
test_eq([lt[0]['s'], lt[0]['e'], lt[1]['s'], lt[1]['e']], [0, 200, 300, 400])
test_eq(lt[2], None)
```

## Reciting sections

A section is recited in parts, each in one voice. By default the section
is split into verses, each closing on a line with a double daṇḍa, and
[ganapati](https://github.com/vedicreader/ganapati) scans each: it
applies the śloka’s rules (Vāgdhenu’s own detector passed a 32-syllable
prose sentence as anuṣṭubh) and knows the āryā family. A metre in
Vāgdhenu’s bank is chanted against its reference, another vṛtta against
the fallback (vasantatilakā), and an āryā-family metre or none is read.
A caller can pass its own parts, `dict(lines=[…], meter=…)`, and `kind`
forces one voice for the whole section. Each part takes the best of
`tries` seeds by Su-śrotā’s error rate.

### shift

``` python

    info, off

```

*Move a section’s timings `off` ms later.*

A stand-in chanter and ear check the bookkeeping without the models: a
verse that scans is chanted, the prose after it is read, and the second
part’s timings start after the first part and the gap.

``` python
from vachaka.core import Recitation
from vachaka.check import Ear
class FakeCh:
    gap, prose_gap = 0.5, 0.3
    def meter(self, lines): return 'anushtubh' if len(lines) == 2 else ''
    def bank_ref(self, name): return {'anuṣṭubh': 'anuṣṭubh', 'mālinī': 'mālinī'}.get(name)
    def render(self, ps, ref, seed, gap): return Recitation(np.zeros(len(ps)*24000, np.float32), [(i*1000, i*1000+900) for i in range(len(ps))], ps)
class FakeEar:
    def hear(self, audio, sr): return ''
    heard = Ear.heard   # best_of hears a render a piece at a time
    def words(self, rec, ws): return [[[w, s, e] for w in p] for (s,e),p in zip(rec.spans, ws)]
r, info = recite_section(FakeCh(), FakeEar(), ['धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।', 'मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥', 'इति प्रश्नः ॥'])
test_eq([p['kind'] for p in info['parts']], ['chant', 'read'])
test_eq(info['kind'], 'mixed')
test_eq(info['lines'][2]['s'], 2000 + 800)           # two 1 s pieces, then the gap
_, info = recite_section(FakeCh(), FakeEar(), ['क ख ग', 'घ ङ च ॥', 'छ ज झ ।'])
test_eq([p['kind'] for p in info['parts']], ['chant', 'read'])  # the line after the verse is its own part, and scans as nothing
ps = [dict(lines=[0, 1], meter='mālinī'), dict(lines=[2], meter='āryā'), dict(lines=[3], meter='śikhariṇī'), dict(lines=[4], meter=None)]
_, info = recite_section(FakeCh(), FakeEar(), ['क ।', 'ख ॥', 'ग ॥', 'घ ॥', 'ङ ।'], parts=ps)
test_eq([(p['kind'], p['ref']) for p in info['parts']], [('chant', 'mālinī'), ('read', 'anuṣṭubh'), ('chant', 'vasantatilaka'), ('read', 'anuṣṭubh')])
```

## CLI

`vachaka-recite jobs.jsonl results.jsonl` renders each job,
`dict(id, out, sections)`, to `out` (mp3 or wav) and appends
`dict(id, out, ms, sections)` to the results. A job already in the
results is skipped, so a stopped run resumes.
